summary_en: FY2027 year-end dividend per share raised from 70 yen to 88 yen, bringing full-year dividend to 158 yen, reflecting upward revision of earnings forecasts driven by higher domestic interest rates boosting net interest income.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Full-Year Performance Forecast and Revision of Year-End Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Nishi-Nippon Financial Holdings has revised its full-year performance forecasts for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, upward and increased the year-end dividend per share accordingly. The company now projects consolidated ordinary income of 77.0 billion yen (previously 69.0 billion yen) and net income attributable to parent company shareholders of 54.0 billion yen (previously 48.0 billion yen). The revision reflects stronger-than-expected net interest income driven by rising domestic interest rates.

In response to the improved earnings outlook, the company has raised its year-end dividend forecast from 70 yen per share to 88 yen per share. Combined with the interim dividend of 70 yen, the full-year dividend is now projected at 158 yen per share, compared to the previous forecast of 140 yen. This compares to actual full-year dividends of 118 yen per share in the prior fiscal year (45 yen interim plus 73 yen year-end).

The dividend increase aligns with the company's stated capital allocation policy, which targets a payout ratio of approximately 40% while seeking dividend growth through profit expansion. The company indicated it will continue to pursue flexible share repurchases based on economic conditions, financial position, and business outlook.
